name: pCloud
summary: Swiss cloud storage for individuals, families and teams, best known for lifetime plans paid once instead of a subscription; includes file sync, versioning, shared folders and links, a media player, and optional client-side encryption as a paid add-on.
best_for: individuals and families who want a large amount of cloud storage for years and would rather pay once than keep a subscription running
skip_if: you need end-to-end encryption by default without an extra purchase, or you are not sure you will still want the same storage in a few years
honest_knock: Client-side encryption is not included in personal plans; it is a separate €150 purchase. The 14-day money-back guarantee comes with a clause that lets pCloud decline refunds on promotional or discounted purchases, and the lifetime prices are presented as discounts. Free accounts inactive for 12 months are deleted with their files, and shared folders only work between accounts in the same data region.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Premium 500 GB Lifetime · one-time payment for 500 GB, read from a Netherlands connection in euros, marked down from €279
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-26 on pcloud.com, its family and business pages, from a Netherlands connection that showed euros; the page calls the prices final) pCloud is best known for lifetime plans paid once. Premium 500 GB is €219 (struck through from €279), Premium Plus 2 TB €499 (from €709) and Ultra 10 TB €1,499 (from €2,799), each a one-time payment that includes pCloud Photos and pCloud Docs and shared-link traffic of twice the storage. Family lifetime plans for up to 5 users cost €749 for 2 TB (from €999) and €1,849 for 10 TB (from €3,499). For teams, Business is €9.99 per user a month with 1 TB per user and Business Pro €14.98 per user a month with 2 TB per user (€44.94 a month for 3 users, marked down from €59.94, for new accounts only), both with a minimum of 3 users and pCloud Encryption included; Business has a 30-day free trial. For personal plans, client-side encryption is a separate add-on: €150 once (from €229). The free account starts with 2 GB and can be unlocked to 10 GB. pCloud also sells monthly and annual Premium plans; we did not record those prices on this read. 'Lifetime' means the account owner's lifetime or 99 years, whichever is shorter. There is a 14-day money-back guarantee, but pCloud reserves the right to decline refunds on promotional or discounted purchases.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We uploaded three files (a CSV and two images) to a private folder, downloaded them back as one ZIP and compared the files byte for byte. We did not open the upgrade or checkout.
findings: The free account started at 2 GB of storage and became 3 GB after our first upload: one extra gigabyte added by that action. The homepage says you can reach up to 10 GB; we only saw the first step.
Upload and download worked even though the email address was not yet confirmed; a banner kept asking for the confirmation.
Selecting three files and choosing Download gave one ZIP with a generic file name. All three files inside were byte-identical to the originals.
Basic account settings report an EU data region. The account-data download explicitly leaves your files out, so it is not a backup of your storage.
No card was asked for in the steps we saw; a lifetime pCloud Pass promotion appeared straight after login.
not_tested: Checkout, tax and the price of the paid plans
The rest of the steps up to 10 GB
Sharing links, invitations and the desktop drive
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
